title: Reverse Bits
pattern: Take the lowest bit, append it to the result
statement: Reverse the bits of a 32-bit unsigned integer `n`: the lowest bit becomes the highest, the second lowest the second highest, and so on.

example.why: 11 is 000…01011. Reversed, the bits read 11010…000, which is 3489660928.

idea: Build the result one bit at a time. `n & 1` reads the **lowest** bit of `n`.
Shift the result **left** by one to make room, and put that bit into the free lowest place. Then shift `n` **right** so its next bit becomes the lowest.
Do this exactly 32 times. The bit read first is pushed left 31 more times and ends up highest — the order is reversed.

steps.text: Our example: **`n = 11`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.

views.title: 32-bit view  (the lowest bit is on the right)

steps.text: `reversed_num` starts empty (all zeros). We will feed it the bits of n, lowest bit first.

views.title: 32-bit view  (the lowest bit is on the right)

steps.text: Round 1: shift the result left by one, then drop in the lowest bit of n, which is **1**.

views.title: 32-bit view  (the lowest bit is on the right)

steps.text: Shift n right by one: the bit just used falls off, and the next bit moves into the lowest place.

steps.text: The same two moves repeat for all 32 bits. n has no 1-bits left, so from now on only zeros are appended — each round still pushes the bits already placed one position further left.

views.title: 32-bit view  (the lowest bit is on the right)

steps.text: After 32 rounds the bit that was lowest has travelled to the highest place: the bits are reversed. As a number: **3489660928**.
